scenarios.title: One link goes viral
scenarios.description: A single short link receives a large share of total traffic within minutes after being shared by a celebrity.
triggers: Traffic to one key grows by orders of magnitude
Cache entry for the key expires during the surge
probes: Where does the extra load land: cache node, database partition, or API tier?
How do you prevent many simultaneous cache misses for the same key?
Does anything in your design assume traffic is evenly distributed across keys?

scenarios.title: Cache layer becomes unavailable
scenarios.description: The cache cluster fails or is restarted and all lookups fall through to the database.
probes: Can the database absorb the full redirect load? Show the calculation.
What protects the database: rate limiting, request coalescing, load shedding, or something else?
How does the system warm the cache after recovery without causing a second overload?

scenarios.title: Primary database failure
scenarios.description: The node accepting writes for part of the key space becomes unavailable.
probes: Which operations keep working: redirects, creation, deletion, analytics?
How is failover performed and what data could be lost or stale?
What does a user see while failover is in progress?

scenarios.title: Ten times the traffic
scenarios.description: Sustained traffic grows tenfold over a quarter.
probes: Which component saturates first, and how do you know?
Which parts of the design scale horizontally without change and which need redesign?
How does cost change, and where would you spend effort first?

scenarios.title: Code collision under concurrency
scenarios.description: Two API servers generate or claim the same short code at nearly the same moment.
probes: Where is uniqueness enforced and what happens to the loser of the race?
How does this behave across multiple regions?
What is the user-visible effect of a retry?

scenarios.title: Analytics pipeline falls behind
scenarios.description: The click-event consumer cannot keep up and the event stream backlog grows.
probes: Is redirect latency or availability affected by the backlog?
What is the backpressure strategy and what is acceptable to drop?
How are duplicate or late events handled?
